headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.8631). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an effect size of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.74–1.11), indicating no statistically significant association between caffeine and uterine cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 60.82%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
